## Why This Is Asked
This question probes the ability to architect a scalable, multi-tenant security model in Kubernetes, balancing native features with a single control plane for runtime enforcement. It assesses identity, policy, and observable security outcomes under real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Pod identity via service accounts and SPIFFE IDs
- Mutual TLS with Istio for east-west and north-south traffic

- NetworkPolicy-based segmentation
- Pod Security Standards and image signing (cosign) in CI/CD
- Telemetry, audits, and validation plans

## Code Example

```yaml
# Istio: mTLS
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: default
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
```
```yaml

  name: namespace-restrict

```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore cosign attestation
- SBOM requirements

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy example
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-sigstore-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: audit
  rules:
  - name: attest-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment, StatefulSet]
    validate:
      message: "image must be cosigned and SBOM present"
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/signature"]: "*"
        metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/sbom"]: "*"
```

```rego
# OPA policy (high level)
package gatekeeper
violation[{"msg": msg}]
default violation = []
violation = [{"msg": m} |
  input.request.kind == "Deployment" and
  not input.request.object.spec.template.metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/signature"]
  or not input.request.object.metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/sbom"] ]
```

- How would you handle SBOM provenance across registries?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement SBOM-based attestations and runtime provenance checks, plus how to wire CI gates with Kosign and CycloneDX.

## Key Concepts

- Image provenance, cosign signatures, attestations
- CycloneDX SBOMs, embedded in image annotations
- GitHub Actions gating, runtime enforcement (Kyverno/OPA)

## Code Example

```yaml
name: prod-provenance
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - manifests/prod/**
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: setup cosign
        run: |
          curl -sSfL https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/download/v1.10.0/cosign-linux-amd64 -o cosign
          chmod +x cosign
          sudo mv cosign /usr/local/bin/
      - name: verify images
        run: |
          cosign verify -key cosign.pub registry.example.com/namespace/service:tag
      - name: verify SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cyclone_dx_attest --image registry.example.com/namespace/service:tag --attest
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle attestation revocation and key rotation?
- How to scale SBOM checks across many services and environments?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of identity-based runtime access control in Kubernetes, integrating SPIRE, OPA Gatekeeper, and admission/mutating webhooks for auditing. It also evaluates plan for cross-cloud (Snowflake/IBM) data workloads and secure Spark job execution.

## Key Concepts
- SPIRE workload identity and attestation
- OPA Gatekeeper constraint templates and validation hooks
- Kubernetes RBAC and API access control
- Mutating webhook for audit sidecars
- Validation strategy with compliant vs noncompliant pods

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (example): OPA-based API access gate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapiaiaccess
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sAPIAccess
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |-
      package k8sapiaiaccess
      violate["API access denied: identity not whitelisted"] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        identity := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["spire.identity"]
        not identity_in_allowlist(identity)
      }
      
      # allowlisted identities (simplified)
      identity_in_allowlist(id) {
        id == "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
      }
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (SPIRE-identity annotated)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-spark
  annotations:
    spire.identity: "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
spec:
  serviceAccountName: spark-sa
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod (no SPIRE identity)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-spark
spec:
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

## Validation Plan
- Deploy constraint template and constraint; attempt compliant pod deployment; verify admission allows and audit sidecar is injected. 
- Deploy noncompliant pod; confirm admission denies with clear event reason. 
- Run a Spark job and inspect API calls logged by the auditing sidecar for traceability.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```

## Why This Question Matters
This tests your ability to design supply chain security for a Kubernetes monorepo where multiple services share base images - a critical skill for CKS certification and real-world cluster security.

## Core Concepts

**Signing vs Attesting:**
- **Signing** (cosign sign): Cryptographically proves an image hasn't been tampered with since it was built and signed
- **Attesting** (cosign attest): Attaches signed metadata (SBOM, provenance) to an image that can be verified later

**SBOM (Software Bill of Materials):**
- Lists all components, packages, and dependencies in an image
- Generated with: `syft image -o spdx-json`
- Standard formats: SPDX, CycloneDX
- Critical for vulnerability scanning and compliance

**SLSA Provenance:**
- Tracks the entire build pipeline (SLSA Level 3+)
- Contains "materials" field that references base image digest
- Enables tracing derived images back to their bases
- Predicate type: `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`

**OCI Referrers:**
- Modern way to store attestations alongside images in OCI-compliant registries
- Replaces older annotation-based approaches
- Supported by Harbor, GHCR, ECR, ACR, GCR

**Policy Enforcement:**
- **Kyverno:** Native Kubernetes policy engine with verifyImages rule
- **OPA/Conftest:** General-purpose policy as code
- Run in CI/CD (before `helm upgrade`) AND optionally as admission controllers

**Key Security Properties:**
1. **Base image integrity:** Verify base images are signed and attested
2. **Derivation chain:** Service images must reference an attested base
3. **Immutable records:** Rekor transparency log ensures no retroactive changes
4. **Automated enforcement:** No deployment without verified images

## Why This Is Asked

It mirrors real-world CI gates used in production environments around Dockerfile hygiene, image signing, SBOM generation, and registry controls. It introduces modern tools like Cosign and SBOM attestations without overwhelming complexity.

## Key Concepts

- **Dockerfile Hygiene**: Non-root USER and multi-stage builds reduce security vulnerabilities and image size
- **Container Image Signing**: Using Cosign to sign and verify container images ensures integrity
- **SBOM Attestation**: Software Bill of Materials provides transparency into image contents and dependencies
- **GitHub Actions Workflows**: Implementing gates and policy checks in CI/CD pipelines
- **Registry Allowlist**: Restricting deployments to approved registries prevents supply chain attacks

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Docker Security Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Validate Dockerfile
        run: |
          # Check for non-root USER
          grep -q 'USER ' Dockerfile || exit 1
          # Check for multi-stage build
          grep -q 'FROM.*AS' Dockerfile || exit 1
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json > sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign image and SBOM with Cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
          cosign attest --type spdx-json --predicate sbom.json ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Verify signature and attestation
        run: |
          cosign verify ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
```
